text: Imagine sorting spiral galaxies into two jars, clockwise and counterclockwise. With no preferred direction, the jars should fill almost evenly. A rotating universe might tip a few extra galaxies into one jar. The test is therefore simple to picture. Classify many galaxies, compare the two totals, and ask whether the imbalance is larger than ordinary counting noise. The hard part is not the counting rule. It is the predicted size.
